findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for SpawnProcess, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: The flusher processes come from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.context.Process`, which is what `multiprocessing.Process` names. The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard is therefore always False for real processes, and `process.kill()` is never called. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. In the `cause == "hang"` case the old process is left running and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second flusher for the same shards. Two flushers then compete over the same Redis keys, which can cause duplicate or fragmented segments and leaked processes. Fix this by checking `hasattr(process, 'kill')`, by checking `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`, or by using `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`. The same wrong check in `join()` means `terminate()` is also never called.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) added to fix a race is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: `test_basic` begins with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)`, commented "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change", calls that patched function and does nothing. The flusher thread therefore still races with `step.join()`, which sets `stopped` right after the drift change, so `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. Wait explicitly instead, for example by polling until `messages` is non-empty with a deadline, or capture the real `time.sleep` before patching.

findings.title: Docstring says one process per shard, but shards are capped and shared
findings.body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard". That is wrong, because `max_processes` caps the process count and shards are distributed round-robin across processes, so one process can serve several shards. The CLI default `--flusher-processes=1` runs a single process for all shards. The `:param topic:` entry is also stale, since no such parameter exists, and `max_processes` is undocumented.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag names (`shard` vs `shards`) for the same shard_tag
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards`. Both carry the same comma-joined value. Dashboards that group or filter by tag will miss one of the two. Pick one name. Also note that the comma-joined list becomes a tag value whose cardinality depends on the shard-to-process assignment.

findings.title: Memory check queries Redis once per flusher buffer on every submit
findings.body: The memory-pressure check in `submit()` used to call `get_memory_info()` on a single buffer. It now calls it on every per-process buffer in `self.buffers`. Assuming `get_memory_info()` reports on the whole Redis cluster rather than only the buffer's assigned shards (not checked here), each call repeats the same `INFO` queries. `submit()` then does up to N times more Redis round trips per batch, and the used/available sums are inflated N-fold, which cancels out in the ratio. Query one buffer, or deduplicate by node, instead.

findings.title: join() breaks out of the loop on deadline without terminating remaining processes
findings.body: When the deadline expires, `join()` does `break`, so the `process.terminate()` call at the bottom of the loop never runs for the remaining processes. They are only reaped as daemons at interpreter exit. Terminating should happen for every process even if the wait budget is exhausted, and the unused `process_index` loop variable can be dropped.

findings.title: No validation of max_processes; negative values crash with KeyError
findings.body: `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` treats 0 as "one per shard", but a negative value from `--flusher-processes -1` (click `type=int` accepts it) is kept. `num_processes = min(-1, n)` is -1, so `process_to_shards_map` is empty and `i % self.num_processes` yields an index that is not in the map, which raises a KeyError at consumer startup. Validate `>= 1`, for example with `click.IntRange(min=1)` on the option.

findings.title: Unused helper _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called; the restart path uses `_create_process_for_shards` directly. It is dead code that adds API surface and a second way to restart processes.

findings.title: New test only checks process bookkeeping, not multi-process flushing or restarts
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` checks only the process count and the shard-to-process map. It never submits spans on multiple shards and checks that segments are flushed, and it never covers the restart, hang or crash paths in `_ensure_processes_alive`, nor the per-process backpressure aggregation. The restart path is where the `isinstance`/`kill` regression lives, and nothing exercises it.
